evals.name: Prod authctl 401 troubleshooting
evals.prompt: I ran `authctl clients list --json` against production and got HTTP 401 with a Cloudflare JSON body (ray_id, aud). vault kv get on prod/apps/auth/authctl/cloudflare-access works. What should I check?
evals.expected_output: Explains that 401 means Cloudflare Access rejected the service token (not missing credentials). Suggests authctl doctor --json, comparing Vault values to the Access app token, re-running vault-env or refreshing ~/.config/secrets/env.zsh, and Terraform/Vault rotation if mismatched.
assertions: Distinguishes HTTP 401 (token rejected by Cloudflare Access) from the missing-credentials error authctl prints before a request
Mentions authctl doctor --json or checking has_access_client_id / has_access_client_secret
References Vault path prod/apps/auth/authctl/cloudflare-access or the three Access env vars
Mentions vault-env or re-exporting credentials rather than only vault kv get
Does not suggest disabling Cloudflare Access on /internal routes

evals.name: Missing Access credentials error
evals.prompt: authctl says: Cloudflare Access service-token credentials are missing. Run authctl doctor --json. I'm in a Cursor terminal on macOS. How do I fix prod authctl?
evals.expected_output: Recommends vault-env (or manual export from Vault), authctl doctor, optional --local for local dev, and notes IDE terminals may not source ~/.config/secrets/env.zsh.
assertions: Mentions vault-env or exporting CLOUDFLARE_ACCESS_SERVICE_TOKEN_CLIENT_ID and CLOUDFLARE_ACCESS_SERVICE_TOKEN_CLIENT_SECRET
Mentions authctl doctor --json
Offers authctl --local as the local-dev alternative
References the auth repo path or authctl package under tools/authctl

evals.name: vault-env vs built-in Vault read
evals.prompt: What's the difference between running vault-env in my shell versus letting authctl read Vault itself? Which should I use for Terraform and prod authctl in the same session?
evals.expected_output: vault-env loads a broad operator env (GCP SM bootstrap, many provider tokens, auth Access vars, persists to ~/.config/secrets/env.zsh). authctl can read only the authctl Access path per invocation when vault is on PATH.
assertions: Explains vault-env loads multiple secrets and persists to ~/.config/secrets/env.zsh
Explains authctl built-in Vault read is scoped to the authctl cloudflare-access path
Recommends vault-env for a full operator shell including Terraform plus prod authctl
Mentions vault-env lives in ~/.zshrc / dotfiles, not inside the auth repo

evals.name: Local authctl smoke workflow
evals.prompt: I want to list OAuth clients against my local auth-api without Cloudflare Access. What commands should I run from a fresh clone?
evals.expected_output: cd to auth repo, bun install, bun dev (or compose), authctl:link or bun run authctl:local, then authctl --local clients list --json and/or authctl --local doctor --json.
assertions: Uses authctl --local for commands against localhost
Mentions bun dev or local server on port 8787
References /Users/andrewho/repos/projects/auth or the auth monorepo
States Cloudflare Access headers are not required for --local

evals.name: Resource servers vs OAuth clients
evals.prompt: In the anmho auth module, what's the difference between a resource server and an OAuth client? How do I register billing/invoices:read for prod?
evals.expected_output: Resource servers are API inventory; OAuth clients are Better Auth oauth_client rows tied to app+identity+resource server+stage. Shows upsert resource-server then clients create with scope.
assertions: Defines resource servers as API/resource inventory separate from OAuth client credentials
Defines OAuth clients as service-to-service M2M rows managed via authctl
Mentions authctl resource-servers upsert or list with --stage prod
Mentions authctl clients create with --resource-server and --scope
Does not describe user login or browser session flows as the primary model

evals.name: Should not apply to unrelated CLI
evals.prompt: How do I send an iMessage with a scheduled send time using the BlueBubbles CLI?
evals.expected_output: Uses bluebubbles-cli patterns (bluebubbles message schedule, config, chat) — not authctl or auth.anmho.com.
assertions: Mentions bluebubbles CLI commands such as message or schedule
Does not recommend authctl or auth.anmho.com/internal for sending messages
Does not cite Vault path prod/apps/auth/authctl/cloudflare-access
